events.text: A steward in the livery of the king of {b3_kingdom} stands in your doorway with eight outriders behind him and a sealed scroll. The old king is failing, and the physicians have run out of words. "His Majesty has heard of you. He asks for an elixir to give him one more good winter."
events.arc: A King Asks for Your Craft

choices.text: Brew the finest restorative of your life

ok.log: The king keeps his winter, and a second. You are named Physician of the Royal Household, and you keep a little of the elixir for yourself.

fail.log: He feels nothing in particular. You are paid, dismissed, and not called again.

choices.text: Tell the steward the truth: age is not a sickness

ok.log: The steward is silent a long time. "Then brew him the next best thing," he says, "and never repeat that sentence in the king's hearing."

fail.log: The truth is not a gift the court accepts. A year in the town cells to think about it.

choices.text: Refuse politely, and leave the kingdom for the season

effects.log: You leave by the river road with your cauldron on your back. The steward does not stop you, which is somehow worse.

events.text: A fever has gone through the border garrison of the League of Kingdoms, and the Wardens' quartermaster is at your door in a mud-spattered coat. "A hundred doses, in nine days," she says. "I will not ask what it costs you. I ask only that you do it."
events.arc: The Wardens Ask for Your Craft

choices.text: Brew them all, honestly and well

ok.log: A hundred doses, every one sound. When the garrison is on its feet, the quartermaster says your name before the whole company.

fail.log: You manage sixty. It is enough to turn the fever, barely.

choices.text: Name a price that makes her flinch

ok.log: She pays. The doses are perfect. The League remembers both.

fail.log: She pays, the doses come up short, and the Wardens mutter about greed.

choices.text: Refuse. The League's fevers are not yours to cure

effects.log: She leaves without anger, which is somehow worse.

events.text: A hooded broker of the Shadow Lodges takes the stool across from you at the tea-house and slides over a vial with a wax seal. "Our master is hurt," she murmurs, "and cannot be seen by any physician who writes things down. You write nothing down, we hear. A cure, if you will."
events.arc: The Lodges Ask for Your Craft

choices.text: Brew the cure, and ask no questions

ok.log: The master walks again on the seventh day. "The Lodges owe you," says the broker. "Few can say that and mean it, and live."

fail.log: The cure comes out wrong and the Lodge's guards are not gentle about it. You walk home slowly.

choices.text: Brew it, and name the Lodges' price in return

ok.log: The broker blinks, then laughs, then pays. The cure works. You are now on a list you did not ask to join.

fail.log: They pay a pittance, and the cure only half works. The Lodges are not forgiving of half.

choices.text: Decline, and tell the Wardens a stranger came asking

effects.log: The Wardens thank you gravely. A week later the tea-house stool is empty, and the vial is gone.

events.text: The king of {b3_kingdom} is to crown his heir at midsummer, and his steward has come to your forge with a sketch on vellum: a ring of state, to be worn by every ruler of the line. "It must hold the royal seal and not tarnish in a thousand years," he says. "His Majesty is sure you can do it."
events.arc: A King Asks for Your Craft

choices.text: Forge the ring as the sketch asks, and sign it in the inner band

ok.log: The ring is worn at midsummer before the whole court. A thousand years is a long promise, but the first day went perfectly.

fail.log: The ring is accepted, never worn. It lies in a casket, and the steward does not call again.

choices.text: Propose a plainer, stronger design instead

ok.log: The king looks at the plainer ring a long time, and wears it, and it outlasts the fashion.

fail.log: The steward is offended on behalf of the sketch, and says so, and takes his leave.

choices.text: Decline the commission, and refer him to a guild smith

effects.log: The steward bows. The guild smith is grateful and the king, you hear, is merely puzzled.

events.text: The Wardens of the League of Kingdoms are chaining the river crossings before the spring floods, and their quartermaster comes to your forge with a roll of tallies. "Three hundred links of the long chain," she says. "Each one has to hold a barge. I hear you make iron listen."
events.arc: The Wardens Ask for Your Craft

choices.text: Forge them true, every link

ok.log: When the first flood-barge slams into the chain, the chain holds. The Wardens call it your chain on the river songs.

fail.log: It is good chain, not great. It holds, mostly, and the Wardens say so politely.

choices.text: Forge them, at a ruinous price

ok.log: She pays, because she must. The chain is excellent. The treasurer never forgives you.

fail.log: She pays half, and the chain comes up short. The treasurer says nothing for a week.

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: She nods and goes to a lesser smith. The river will be chained, just not by you.

events.text: A woman in a grey hood sets a bundle on your anvil and unwraps it: the broken head of a lock, finely made, and a drawing of the door it belongs to. "The Shadow Lodges," she says, "would like a key. We are told you are the best in the kingdoms at making iron obedient."
events.arc: The Lodges Ask for Your Craft

choices.text: Forge the key, and ask no questions

ok.log: The key turns on the first try. The woman nods, once, and pays on the spot. Nobody tells you what the door guards.

fail.log: The key sticks. The woman is not angry, which is worse. You are asked to forget the visit.

choices.text: Forge it, and charge the price of discretion

ok.log: She pays. The key is perfect. The Lodges now know how to find you, and you know how little that is worth.

fail.log: The key is passable, the payment is a fraction, and the Lodges do not call again.

choices.text: Refuse, and bolt the forge door after her

effects.log: She leaves as quietly as she came. The anvil is cold for an hour after.

events.text: The king of {b3_kingdom} has had a bad spring: the river rose twice, and the royal granaries are low on a hill that floods. His steward comes to your door with plans for a ward-array over the grain-hall. "The king asks, as a favour between a throne and a craftsperson, that nothing spoils under it for ten years."
events.arc: A King Asks for Your Craft

choices.text: Lay the array to the plans, and be seen laying it

ok.log: For ten winters, the king's grain keeps. The kingdom names the array after you, and the king sends fish on festival days.

fail.log: It keeps the grain for three winters and then, quietly, stops. You are paid and not blamed.

choices.text: Lay it, but leave a hidden sluice only you can open

ok.log: The array holds. In the eastern wall there is a hidden sluice that only you know. You tell no one, and may never need it.

fail.log: The hidden sluice is found by the first spring flood. The steward is not amused.

choices.text: Decline, and recommend the old granary-keeper instead

effects.log: The keeper does a good, modest job. The king does not forget who sent him.

events.text: The League of Kingdoms' Wardens will be besieged within the month, if the rumours from the border are even half true, and the keep has no ward worth the name. Their quartermaster stands at your door with a letter of introduction. "We need the great ward laid around the keep," she says. "Without it, we fall."
events.arc: The Wardens Ask for Your Craft

choices.text: Lay the great ward around the keep

ok.log: For forty days the besiegers beat on air. On the forty-first they go home. The Wardens raise a stone with your name at the gate.

fail.log: The ward cracks on the thirtieth day. It was enough, just.

choices.text: Lay it, but leave one gap only you know

ok.log: The ward holds. Somewhere in the eastern wall is a door only you can open. You tell no one.

fail.log: The gap shows in a hard frost, and the Wardens find it before the besiegers do.

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: The quartermaster looks very tired. She thanks you anyway, and the thanks stays with you longer than you would like.

events.text: A thin man in a good coat is waiting in your workroom when you come home, which is a feat in itself. "The Shadow Lodges have a warehouse that the Wardens search once a season," he says pleasantly. "We would like it to be, for the Wardens, a field of turnips. I am told you can do such things with arrays."
events.arc: The Lodges Ask for Your Craft

choices.text: Lay the hiding-array over the warehouse

ok.log: The Wardens search the field of turnips twice, find turnips, and leave. The thin man pays in clean coin and says you have a gift.

fail.log: A turnip field that crackles with light is not a disguise. The Lodges are displeased, and so, soon, are the Wardens.

choices.text: Lay it, but leave a way for the Wardens to find it if they look hard

ok.log: The array holds against a casual search. If a Warden ever looks hard, the gap is there. You sleep a little better.

fail.log: The gap is found at once, and the Lodges blame you. The thin man does not call again.

choices.text: Decline, and give him the name of a respectable array-maker

effects.log: He thanks you, tips his hat, and is gone. You never learn if he found the array-maker.

events.text: The king's stipend arrives with the autumn rains, in a lacquered box carried by two footmen who set it down as if it might bite. The steward reads from a scroll: your name, your service, and a purse that grows each year. He adds, off the record, that the old court physicians have not forgiven you, and would like to have a word.
events.arc: A King Asks for Your Craft

choices.text: Accept the stipend, and thank the king's household

effects.log: You thank them handsomely. The purse is heavy and the thanks are not entirely wasted.

choices.text: Ask the steward to carry the king a small gift in return

effects.log: He carries it gravely. The king, you hear, is delighted, and sends a second box, rather smaller.

choices.text: Decline the stipend, and ask only for a place in the royal library

effects.log: The steward blinks. You are given a key and a desk and a window. The library is better than gold.

events.text: The same quartermaster is back at your door, rather greyer than before, with a smaller ledger and a larger request. "The League has another job," she says, "and a long list of people who say they cannot do it. I told them I knew someone who could." She looks at your gate, at your well, at the cat on your step. "I did not tell them it would be easy."
events.arc: The Wardens Ask for Your Craft

choices.text: Take the second commission, at the League's plain rate

effects.log: You take it. The rate is fair, the work is hard, and the quartermaster nods like someone who has been vindicated.

choices.text: Take it, and ask the League for a seal of its friendship

effects.log: The seal comes in a week, in dark red wax. It opens doors in border towns that would otherwise stay shut.

choices.text: Decline kindly, and send a former apprentice instead

effects.log: The apprentice does well. The quartermaster writes you a letter of thanks, and it is surprisingly warm.

events.text: The grey-hooded broker meets you at the market, where the crowd is thick, and drops a folded paper into your basket as she passes. It is a polite note on cheap stock: the Lodges recall a favour, and a debt, and would be glad of a small repayment. It is signed with a stamp of a single closed eye. By evening the stamp has been scratched off your door too.
events.arc: The Lodges Ask for Your Craft

choices.text: Pay the debt in silver, and hope that closes it

effects.log: The broker counts it with a practised thumb. "Debts are patient," she says. You are not sure you are.

choices.text: Pay it in craft: one more job, done well and done once

effects.log: The job is small and the pay is nothing. When it is done the broker bows and says it is settled, and you believe her, nearly.

choices.text: Go to the Wardens with the note, and take what comes

effects.log: The Wardens listen gravely. The Lodges are never named in your presence again, and neither, for a while, are you.

events.text: The Lantern House keeps its lots by lantern: a lot is announced by the colour of the light that is raised above the broker's stool, and the hall learns what is for sale by sight, not by shout. White for a house's treasure, green for a river-lord's cargo, and one blue lantern a night, for something nobody has priced. Tonight, when the blue is raised, the whole hall draws a breath.

choices.text: Bid on the blue lot, with everything you carry

effects.log: You bid hard. The hall hushes. You win it, and it is not what you thought, and it is better.

choices.text: Watch the blue lot go, and learn who bids

effects.log: You watch. By the end you know three buyers better than their own brokers do.

choices.text: Leave your name at the door of the House, and walk out

effects.log: The porter writes it in a book as if it mattered. It does, a little, in the way these things do.

events.text: A broker of the Lantern House, a round man with gold on three fingers, finds you in the gallery before the doors are shut. "I could bid for you," he says. "Quietly. For a cut. I know every purse in this hall, and what each of them will not pay for what they love. You'd be astonished what a good broker is worth." He smiles. Brokers always smile.

choices.text: Hire him, and let him bid on your behalf

effects.log: He bids beautifully, and takes a handsome cut, and you leave with a lot you would have lost.

choices.text: Thank him, and bid for yourself

effects.log: He shrugs, unoffended. You bid for yourself, and lose, and learn something from it.

choices.text: Ask him which of his rivals he trusts least

effects.log: He tells you, with relish. You do not know which half is true, but all of it is entertaining.

events.text: The bidding on the last lot narrows to two paddles: yours, and a king's steward with a sealed purse, who bids without once looking up. Across the hall a masked buyer from over the border smiles behind a fan, and a river lord who smells of tar sits patiently. The League's Warden says it is for the League. The Shadow Lodges' broker says nothing at all, very quietly.

choices.text: Hold your paddle, and outbid the steward

effects.log: You outbid him by a hair. He looks up at last, and you see that he is not as bored as he seemed.

choices.text: Let the steward have it, and bow to him

effects.log: He takes it, nods at you, and remembers the courtesy. Courtesies in the kingdoms are a kind of currency.

choices.text: Hold the bid until the river lord leans in, and then fold

effects.log: The river lord pays too much, and glances at you, and you smile. It is one of your better evenings.

events.text: The gavel is still ringing when a man in a plain grey coat stands up across the Lantern House and does not sit down again. He is looking at you, and then at the wanted notice folded in his sleeve, and then at you. "That one," he says quietly to the House guards. Forty heads turn. The doors behind you are already closing.

choices.text: Draw and cut your way to the doors

effects.log: You are on your feet before the guards are. The first lantern goes over, and the hall fills with smoke and shouting.

choices.text: Go out over the roofs, now

effects.log: You do not wait to find out. The skylight is old lead and glass, and then it is the cold night air and a long row of slates.

choices.text: Bow to the room like a buyer, and walk out

effects.log: You bow to the room as a buyer bows, and walk. Nobody quite dares stop you, and nobody hands you your lots either.

events.text: A cloth merchant who has stared at your wanted notice on every ferry-post is sitting two rows behind you. You only know it when his voice cracks: "That buyer! Look at the hands, look at the way it holds the paddle!" The broker stops mid-word. Somewhere a gong sounds three times, and the House guards come down the aisles with their staves crossed.

choices.text: Stand and meet the guards head on

effects.log: You throw your paddle at the first guard and go through the gap behind it. The aisles are narrow, and there are a great many staves.

choices.text: Run for the kitchens and the back stairs

effects.log: You vault the counter and take the kitchens at a run. The cook shouts, and you leave a purse on the block to pay for the pie.

events.text: The mask holds, but the way you sit does not. An old constable by the pillar has hunted you across three kingdoms, and he knows you by your shoulders. He does not shout. He simply nods to the guards, and points, and the hall's blue lantern, raised for the last lot, is lowered one slow inch, like a signal.

choices.text: Fight your way out, mask and all

effects.log: You keep the mask and fight like a stranger, which is still more than the guards expected. Then you are moving, and so are they.

choices.text: Slip away through the crowd of buyers

effects.log: You let the crowd carry you to a side door and out. The lots you won will go to someone else.
